title: Two ants at the rock edge

source.original_plan_why_this_clip: One black ant in side view walks slowly along a rock edge in the middle of the frame, stepping its legs and turning slightly. The clip has no cuts; the interval ends at 2.25 s before a second ant enters and overlaps it from below.
source.why_this_clip: Two ants face one another and alter antenna reach at a rock gap. The retained interval excludes the initial cut; the original one-ant description is rejected.
source.plan_correction: The first raw frame is another shot. Two ants, not one, are visible throughout the retained interval. Both are represented. No claim that a second ant enters only at2.25s is retained as observation.
source.why_this_interval: Eighteen preflight samples locate a cut before0.04s and show two ants facing and moving their antennae from0.2 to2.2s. The retained interval is continuous in sampled frames; actual normal-speed approval is unrun.

assembly_summary: Two copies of the same eleven-stroke ant follow observed three-part body positions and unequal antenna/leg reaches. The five-legged simplification is preserved; no material contact identity or touching event is asserted from a mask. One held rock plate follows background-only registration.
